details: The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has proposed a new regulatory framework, "Regulation Crypto Assets," aimed at providing clear pathways for crypto companies to raise capital. This proposal includes exemptions for certain crypto offerings from existing securities rules, allowing for one-time exemptions up to $5 million over four years and up to $75 million annually with reporting requirements. SEC Chair Paul Atkins stated this is a step towards onshoring innovation in crypto markets.
title: US SEC Proposes New Crypto Asset Regulations

details: Bitcoin has shown cautious movement, with some reports indicating a drop of over 2% within a 24-hour period due to ongoing economic uncertainty. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index is in the "fear" category, reflecting current market sentiment. While there have been minor recoveries, the overall short-term trend indicates bears remain in control, with predictions suggesting a potential drop below the $62,000 support level.
title: Bitcoin Trades Cautiously Amid Market Uncertainty

details: President Donald Trump is expected to host executives from prominent crypto firms such as Coinbase, Ripple, and Kraken at the White House on August 19. SEC Chairman Paul Atkins and CFTC's Mike Selig are also anticipated to attend these regulatory meetings. The discussions are likely to focus on the future of crypto regulation, particularly concerning the stalled CLARITY Act.
title: White House to Host Crypto Industry Leaders for Regulatory Talks

details: Cryptocurrency exchange Bybit has significantly upgraded its security infrastructure, incorporating expanded account protection, 100% on-chain monitoring, and AI-assisted threat detection. In the first half of 2026, Bybit successfully intercepted over 30,000 suspicious withdrawal requests, safeguarding nearly 20,000 users from potential losses exceeding $700 million. This follows a previous security incident in February 2025.
title: Bybit Enhances Security, Prevents $700M in Potential Losses
